note: Flat sanctoral. Every entry carries an explicit `observance` rule: fixed | cycle | ordinal. `dayLegacy` preserves the original month-file day string for audit. `ruleSource` records the evidence for any non-default rule; an entry without one is a fixed date inherited from the previous data and NOT independently confirmed against a printed calendar. An entry with an empty `tags` array is a retained-but-unsourced identity. CORRECTED 2026-09-12: this sentence previously said such entries carry a `tagsGap` field stating why and that 170 entries were in that state. NO entry carries a `tagsGap` field -- the count is zero, checked directly -- and exactly TWO entries have an empty `tags` array (`saint-mark-of-ephesus`, `saints-sarbelus-and-barbea`). The 170 figure described the state of the file immediately after the 2026-09-03 Layer 3 sourcing pass and was never updated as those rows were re-sourced or removed. Such entries never resolve and never display. They are not dead data to be swept: they are the disclosed remains of the 2026-09-03 Layer 3 sourcing pass, kept so they can be re-sourced. SCHEMA, extended 2026-09-05: an entry may carry an optional `traditionObservance` map of tradition code to observance rule. One identity is often kept on DIFFERENT DAYS by different traditions — Benedict of Nursia is 11 July for the Episcopal Church and 14 March in the East — and the schema previously allowed one row to hold several tradition tags but only ONE date, which forced either a date that is wrong for some of the row's own tags or a duplicate row per tradition. When a resolver asks on behalf of a tradition listed in `traditionObservance`, that rule applies; otherwise the shared `observance` does. The field is optional and additive, so every entry without it behaves exactly as before. LFF controls the ANG date in every case. SCHEMA, extended 2026-09-07: an OOR-tagged entry may carry an optional `oorSubtradition` string naming which Oriental Orthodox church its content actually belongs to -- "Armenian", "Ethiopian", "Syriac", etc. OOR's governing confirmation source is Coptic Reader/coptic.io specifically (Josh, 2026-09-05); CORRECTED 2026-09-12, and this correction is load-bearing: this sentence previously said an entry with no `oorSubtradition` is implicitly Coptic and is checked against that source. That is WRONG and a filter built on it hides real content. Absence means the row is NOT sub-tradition-specific -- it applies to all of them. 62 of the unscoped OOR rows are shared with ANG/LAT/EOR/COE and are pan-Christian (Epiphany, the Circumcision, Basil the Great, Matthias, the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste); reading absence as Coptic would hide every one of them from Armenian, Syriac and Ethiopian users. The genuinely Coptic-only rows were explicitly marked `Coptic` on 2026-09-12, so absence now means what it says. The shipped resolver (`appliesToSubtradition()` in js/saints-resolver.js) and the Office Settings sub-tradition picker both implement THESE semantics, not the old sentence's -- do not "correct" either of them back toward it. What remains true from the old sentence: OOR's governing confirmation source for an unscoped or Coptic-marked row is Coptic Reader/coptic.io specifically (Josh, 2026-09-05). An entry WITH `oorSubtradition` set to something other than Coptic is real content for that sub-tradition, not a Coptic-calendar mismatch -- it must not be checked against coptic.io, corrected toward a Coptic date, withdrawn, or deleted on the strength of a Coptic-source no-match. It stays OOR-tagged (OOR is the parent/Oriental-Orthodox tag) and awaits its own tradition's governing source, expected as this project expands into other Oriental Orthodox sub-traditions (Josh, 2026-09-07).

entries.name: Saint James The Brother Of The Lord
entries.description: James, brother of the Lord, first Bishop of Jerusalem -- commemorated jointly with the Blessed Virgin Mary. Source: the ACOE Diocese of California 2026 calendar. This is the Church of the East's own distinct commemoration date for this figure, different from (and not intended to replace) the separate Apr.30 and Oct.23 dates already present in this corpus for other traditions -- different traditions commemorating the same figure on different days is normal practice throughout this corpus, not an inconsistency to resolve.
entries.ruleSource: The LAST FRIDAY BEFORE the Epiphany, commemorated with the Blessed Virgin Mary and named as the first Bishop of Jerusalem: 5 Jan 2024, 2 Jan 2026. 2/2. Expressed with a negative n (count backward from the anchor). A first attempt used a forward count from Epiphany minus seven days; that resolved to NOTHING in three years of twenty and to TWO days in four others, because the forward count can overshoot the feast. Caught by the resolvability sweep. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars (2026 and 2024 in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021). DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Commemoration of All the Saints
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 November 15, 2026 November 15. Across those years it resolves to a FIXED date, identical in every year held, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Commemoration of Mar Benyamin Shimun XXI
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 February 4, 2026 February 8. Across those years it resolves to a fixed offset of -56 days from the Resurrection, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.eorDateNote: STRUCTURAL FIX 2026-09-07: EOR keeps Joseph the Betrothed, David the King and James the Brother of the Lord on the Sunday after Nativity, not a fixed date -- the shared Mar 19 date is Western tradition's, left untouched for ANG/LAT. When there is no Sunday within this period, we celebrate this commemoration on the 26th" -- the rare case when Christmas itself falls on a Sunday, which would otherwise push the naive search into January and collide with the Circumcision/Basil the Great feast. Implemented as a new bounded-window-with-fallback extension to the 'relative' observance type (js/saints-resolver.js), tested programmatically across 2020-2035 including both years in that range where Christmas falls on a Sunday (2022, 2033) before this change was made.

entries.name: St. Mari the Bishop
entries.description: STRUCTURALLY MOVABLE, not an unresearched gap: Maclean's own Kalendar appendix (p.264-283) gives Mar Mari, disciple of Mar Addai tied only to the movable pre-Fast Friday cycle -- confirmed independently by both the ACOE Diocese of California and ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe 2026 calendars, which both place this same commemoration on a Friday that shifts year to year (Feb.6 in 2026 specifically). The same cycle already computed by getPreFastSundayFoldSchedule() in js/calendar-east-syriac.js (deliberately unwired). No fixed Gregorian date exists for this commemoration in this tradition. Distinct from mar-mari-the-apostle (already sourced, July 24, Maclean's own separate, fixed entry for the apostolic founder figure) where the id refers to Mari the disciple of Addai specifically.
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 January 5, 2026 January 2. Across those years it resolves to the 1st Friday of January, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.description: RESOLVED as a duplicate allowlist id for an already-sourced identity, mar-addai (May 3) -- deliberately left without a COE tag on any occurrence of this id, since tagging both would display the same person twice on the same date. Not an unresearched gap.
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 April 28, 2026 May 3. Across those years it resolves to a fixed offset of +28 days from the Resurrection, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Daniel The Physician
entries.description: Mar Daniel the Physician. Identity verified. NOT A FIXED DATE, and its grouping also varies: the 2026 edition commemorates him with Mar Addai (Thaddeus) the Apostle on 3 May, while the 2025 edition commemorates him on 4 May with Mar Abdisho, Mar Jonah the Ascetic and Mar Ananias. The date stored here is the 2026 date. Source: Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe, Diocesan Ecclesiastical Calendar (English), acote.church/ecclesiastical-calendar
entries.ruleSource: UNSTABLE ACROSS ALL SEVEN EDITIONS, deliberately left as a fixed date and flagged rather than given an invented rule. Mar Daniel the Physician moves AND changes company every year, occupying FOUR different slots: Sunday of Resurrection week 4 in 2020 (alone); week 5 in 2021, 2023 and 2026 (with Mar Addai); week 3 in 2022 and 2025 (with Mar Abdisho, Mar Yonan and Mar Khanania, and in 2022 also Mar Abimalek Timotheus); week 6 in 2024 (alone). Three years at week 5, two at week 3, one each at weeks 4 and 6. No slot commands a majority and no rule is derivable from the source. The stored 3 May is the 2026 date and is wrong in five of the seven years. Resolving this needs a judgement about which commemoration the entry is actually tracking, not more data. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars, ALL SEVEN editions 2020-2026 read in full.

entries.name: St. Andrew the Apostle
entries.description: One of the Twelve Apostles. (ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026.)
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 November 30, 2026 November 30. Across those years it resolves to a FIXED date, identical in every year held, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Mari the Apostle
entries.description: Commemoration of the teacher of the East.
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 July 19, 2026 July 24. Across those years it resolves to a fixed offset of +110 days from the Resurrection, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Abraham
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 May 2, 2026 May 2. Across those years it resolves to a FIXED date, identical in every year held, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Mushi
entries.description: The Old Testament figure Moses -- 'the Firstborn of the Prophets,' per the ACOE Diocese of California 2026 calendar, the only source found giving this identity a specific commemoration day. Disclosed rather than asserted with full confidence: the allowlist also carries other, more specific historical 'Mar Moses' figures elsewhere (of Chalek, of Beth Sayyare) not connected to this generic id, and Mushi/Mushe is the standard Syriac form of Moses -- this reading (the biblical Moses, not a later monastic of the same name) is the best-supported one available but not independently cross-confirmed by a second source. The identity id was previously scattered across three different unsourced dates (Jul.19, Aug.28, Sept.13) with no citation for any of them -- all stripped.
entries.ruleSource: Mar Moses, the Firstborn of the Prophets. THE CORRECT RULE IS KNOWN BUT CANNOT CURRENTLY BE EXPRESSED. California places this in the FIRST WEEK OF MOSES -- Mar Mushi on its Sunday (17 Oct 2021, 13 Oct 2024, 18 Oct 2026) and St Jacob the Recluse on its Friday (22 Oct 2021, 18 Oct 2024, 23 Oct 2026), both 3/3. Encoding that as a cycle rule was tried and REVERTED: js/calendar-east-syriac.js fails to produce a Muse week 1 in 5 years out of 20, because Muse is squeezed between an Eliya season built forward from Easter and a Hallowing season fitted backward from Subara, and can collapse to zero weeks. A rule that resolves to nothing makes the commemoration DISAPPEAR from the app, which is worse than a wrong date. Held as a fixed date (the 2026 value) until the season-collision defect is fixed -- see the dashboard row coe:engine:season-collision-2038, whose scope is far wider than the 2 years in 81 first measured. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars (2026 and 2024 in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021). DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Saint Luke the Evangelist

entries.name: Saint Jacob The Recluse
entries.description: St. Jacob the Recluse -- distinct from Jacob of Nisibis and Jacob the Mutilated, both separately commemorated elsewhere in this corpus.
entries.ruleSource: St Jacob the Recluse. THE CORRECT RULE IS KNOWN BUT CANNOT CURRENTLY BE EXPRESSED. California places this in the FIRST WEEK OF MOSES -- Mar Mushi on its Sunday (17 Oct 2021, 13 Oct 2024, 18 Oct 2026) and St Jacob the Recluse on its Friday (22 Oct 2021, 18 Oct 2024, 23 Oct 2026), both 3/3. Encoding that as a cycle rule was tried and REVERTED: js/calendar-east-syriac.js fails to produce a Muse week 1 in 5 years out of 20, because Muse is squeezed between an Eliya season built forward from Easter and a Hallowing season fitted backward from Subara, and can collapse to zero weeks. A rule that resolves to nothing makes the commemoration DISAPPEAR from the app, which is worse than a wrong date. Held as a fixed date (the 2026 value) until the season-collision defect is fixed -- see the dashboard row coe:engine:season-collision-2038, whose scope is far wider than the 2 years in 81 first measured. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars (2026 and 2024 in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021). DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Rabban Mar Bar Edta
entries.ruleSource: Friday of the Fourth Week of the Hallowing of the Church: 29 Nov 2024 and 27 Nov 2026. 2/2. Was a fixed 27 November, which is the 2026 date only. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars (2026 and 2024 in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021). DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Michael
entries.ruleSource: Date DERIVED 2026-09-06 from the printed Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars held in data/kalendar/source-witnesses/ (2024 and 2026 in full; the June, August, September and October 2021 pages, read by OCR). This commemoration is printed on: 2024 March 17, 2026 March 22. Across those years it resolves to a fixed offset of -14 days from the Resurrection, and the rule is stored in that form rather than as a fixed date. WHY THAT MATTERS: this row previously carried a FIXED date, and a fixed date can never match a commemoration that moves — which is why every calendar match run against these rows failed and why they looked unsourceable. The fault was the rule TYPE, not the absence of a source. Derived from 2 printed years; two years can fit a rule by coincidence, so a two-year derivation is weaker than a three-year one and is stated as such here. DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.description: Sabrisho of Beth Qoqa (or Beth Garmai). Confirmed at this date by two independent sources: the ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe 2026 calendar ('St. Sawrisho of Beth Qoqa, St. Steven, St. Khnana') and the ACOE Diocese of California 2026 calendar ('Mar Sabrisho of Bet-Qoqa'). The identity id was previously scattered across three different unsourced dates (Jul.18, Aug.20, Sept.12) with no citation for any of them -- all stripped.
entries.ruleSource: Mar Sawrisho of Beth Qoqa. NOT CLEANLY RULED. California gives 6 Oct 2024 and 4 Oct 2026 (both the first Sunday of October) but 2 Oct 2021, which is a SATURDAY and the day before that year's first Sunday. The ordinal rule holds 2/3 in California. Western Europe gives the first Sunday of October 7/7, so the rule is right and 2021 California looks like a local variation or a printing slip. Kept as the ordinal rule with the discrepancy disclosed rather than smoothed away. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of California ecclesiastical calendars (2026 and 2024 in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021). DIOCESAN SCOPE, established 2026-09-06 and not assumed: this rule is the DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA's reckoning, not the Church of the East's universally. The Assyrian Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's 2026 calendar (Christ the Good Shepherd, Wakeley) was parsed and compared against California 2026 for the same year, and the two dioceses disagree in two consistent ways. Fixed feasts sit THIRTEEN DAYS later at Wakeley — Epiphany on 19 January against 6, All Saints on 28 November against 15, Mar Jacob on 2 December against 19 — which is the Julian reckoning, and is exactly what the fixedFeastMode option in js/calendar-east-syriac.js already exists to model. Week-anchored commemorations sit ONE WEEK later — Mar Addai, Mar Mari, Mar Ezekiel, Prophet Elijah and the Greek and Assyrian Doctors all +7 days. So a date read from one diocese must not be presented as the Church's, and these rules are labelled Californian rather than left to be mistaken for universal.

entries.name: Mar Yosip Khnanisho
entries.description: Mar Yosip Khnanisho, Metropolitan of Shemsdin (1893-1977). Identity verified. NOT A FIXED DATE: kept on the second Sunday of July (12 Jul 2026, 13 Jul 2025); in 2026 this coincided with the Feast of Nusardel, in 2025 it did not. The date stored here is the 2026 date. Source: Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe, Diocesan Ecclesiastical Calendar (English), acote.church/ecclesiastical-calendar
entries.ruleSource: The second Sunday of July. Verified against the Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars 2020-2026, all seven editions (7/7). Coincided with the Feast of Nusardel in 2026 but not in other years.

entries.name: St. Zaia the Blessed
entries.description: ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026. A Rogation (preparatory commemoration) for the same saint is kept Jan.5, and he is commemorated again jointly with others Sept.14.
entries.ruleSource: The first Wednesday of January: 1 Jan 2020, 6 Jan 2021, 5 Jan 2022, 4 Jan 2023, 3 Jan 2024, 7 Jan 2026. 6/6 in the years that carry the commemoration; the 2025 edition has only the optional Rogation of St Zaia on 1 January and no commemoration at all. CORRECTED 2026-09-03: an earlier pass, working from five editions, made this 'the Wednesday nearest the Epiphany'. That matched 2021-2024 and 2026 but is WRONG for 2020, where the commemoration falls on 1 January and the nearest Wednesday to the Epiphany would be 8 January. The coincidence held for four consecutive years and broke on the fifth -- a direct demonstration of why a rule is not derived until every available edition has been checked. Distinct from the fixed 14 September commemoration, where St Zaia is named with St Sawa and others. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars, ALL SEVEN editions 2020-2026 read in full.

entries.name: Prophet Elias Elijah
entries.description: The Old Testament prophet Elijah the Tishbite. Confirmed at this date by two independent sources: the ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe 2026 calendar ('St. Elijah the Tishbite') and the ACOE Diocese of California 2026 calendar ('Prophet Mar Elijah the Teshbite'). The identity id previously carried other traditions' tags (EOR, OOR) at July 20 with no COE tag or citation -- COE not added there, since the Church of the East's own calendar gives a different date.
entries.ruleSource: Friday of the Seventh Week of Elijah. Verified against the Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars 2020-2026, all seven editions (7/7).

entries.name: Saint Andrew the Apostle
entries.description: One of the Twelve Apostles. CORRECTED 2026-08-30: the ACOE Diocese of California 2026 calendar gives Nov.30 for this figure -- the near-universal date across Christian traditions generally, and a stronger, more independently corroborated date than the May.17 date this project had originally sourced from the ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe 2026 calendar alone. COE tag moved from the May.17 entry to this one.
entries.ruleSource: 30 November in 2024 and 2026 -- 2/2. CONFIRMS the earlier revert. Western Europe keeps St Andrew on the Sunday of the Week After Ascension; California keeps the fixed 30 November. A genuine divergence between two dioceses of the same church, and this project follows California. Assyrian Church of the East, DIOCESE OF CALIFORNIA ecclesiastical calendars -- the 2026 and 2024 editions in full, plus the June, August, September and October pages of 2021. EOR separately CONFIRMED 2026-09-07 against orthocal.info (Slavic tradition, OCA/ROCOR practice): “Holy, Glorious and Illustrious Apostle Andrew the First-Called” on this date. The COE confirmation above does not by itself confirm EOR.
entries.oorDateNote: OOR date CORRECTED via traditionObservance 2026-09-07; MOVED to this row 2026-09-12. The override was originally written to the OTHER row sharing this id -- the COE-only ACOTE row -- which carries no OOR tag, so it could never fire. This row is the one that actually holds the OOR tag. Shared date (Nov 30) is ANG/LAT/EOR/COE's. CONFIRMED against coptic.io: "The Martyrdom of St. Andrew the Apostle, the Brother of St. Peter" falls Dec 13 (4 Kiahk).

entries.name: St. Jacob of Nisibis
entries.description: 4th-century bishop of Nisibis, teacher of Mar Ephraim. (ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026.)
entries.ruleSource: Friday of the First Week of Summer. Verified against the Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars 2020-2026, all seven editions (7/7). Falls in August in 2025 and July otherwise.

entries.name: St. John the Baptist
entries.description: Forerunner of Christ. ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026. Distinct from this file's own Jan.7 'Synaxis of John the Baptist' and the June/August/September commemorations of specific events in his life (Nativity, Martyrdom, Conception) already present elsewhere in this corpus -- multiple distinct annual commemorations of the same figure are normal practice, not duplication.
entries.ruleSource: The first Friday after the Epiphany: 10 Jan 2020, 8 Jan 2021, 7 Jan 2022, 13 Jan 2023 (the Epiphany itself fell on a Friday, so the following one), 12 Jan 2024, 10 Jan 2025, 9 Jan 2026. 7/7. Anchored to the Epiphany, not to a week of a season -- the same commemoration falls inside the Nativity weeks in some years and the Epiphany weeks in others, so no cycle rule can hold it. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars, ALL SEVEN editions 2020-2026 read in full.

entries.name: Saint Shamuni and Sons
entries.description: Mother of the seven Maccabean martyrs (2 Macc. 7); called Shmuni/Shamuni in Syriac tradition, Solomonia in Greek -- the same figure, per the standard scholarly identification. ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe Ecclesiastical Calendar 2026 gives this date as 'St. Solomonia and her sons'; the same diocesan calendar also keeps a separate annual commemoration May 5, not represented as a second dated entry here since no distinct id exists in the allowlist for it -- noted for the record rather than silently dropped.
entries.ruleSource: St Shmuni (Solomonia) and her sons, the Friday of the Fifth Week of Summer: 21 Aug 2020, 13 Aug 2021, 26 Aug 2022, 18 Aug 2023, 9 Aug 2024, 14 Aug 2026. 6/7. The single miss is 2025, which places her on Saturday 16 August in the third week of Summer -- the same compression year in which the diocese merged the Sixth and Seventh Weeks of Summer. NOTE: a SECOND commemoration of the same saint falls in spring, on the first Tuesday of May (5 May 2020, 4 May 2021, 3 May 2022, 2 May 2023, 7 May 2024, 6 May 2025, 5 May 2026 -- 7/7). Only the August one is modelled here; the spring one is not in this corpus. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars, ALL SEVEN editions 2020-2026 read in full.

entries.name: Saints Peter And Paul Apostles
entries.description: SS. Peter and Paul. Source: Maclean 1894 (p.282-283, Kashkul MS list) and the ACOTE Diocese of Western Europe 2026 calendar, both independently giving this date -- already gathered in this project's own earlier research but never actually entered into the corpus until now. Distinct from the movable pre-Fast Friday joint commemoration of Peter&Paul with the Four Evangelists (deliberately not sourced here, since that date shifts year to year with the Denkha season length -- see the pre-Fast fold-schedule work).
entries.ruleSource: CORRECTED 2026-09-03. Was a fixed 29 July, which appears in no edition -- the commemoration is in JANUARY. The second Friday after the Epiphany: 17 Jan 2020, 15 Jan 2021, 14 Jan 2022, 20 Jan 2023, 19 Jan 2024, 17 Jan 2025, 16 Jan 2026. 7/7, exactly one week after St John the Baptist in every edition. The Four Evangelists are named with them in 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2026 and commemorated separately a week later in 2022 and 2025 -- that grouping is editorial. Assyrian Church of the East, Diocese of Western Europe published ecclesiastical calendars, ALL SEVEN editions 2020-2026 read in full.

entries.name: Holy Prophet Azariah
entries.description: Old Testament prophet, son of Oded, who prophesied to King Asa of Judah (2 Chronicles 15) -- distinct from Azariah/Abednego of the Three Holy Youths.
entries.ruleSource: RESTORED 2026-09-07: this row was deleted during the EOR sanctoral pass (2026-09-07) on the finding of 'no Orthodox attestation found under any phrasing tried' against orthocal.info. Found afterward via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Feb 3, itself citing Pravoslavie.ru and Ecclesia.gr (the Greek Church's own calendar site) -- both primary-adjacent Orthodox calendar sources, not just a compiled encyclopedia entry. This was a false negative from orthocal.info's search coverage, not a genuine absence -- same category as the Clement of Rome case (EOR pass) and the Ephrem/Beheading-of-John-the-Baptist cases (OOR pass). Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info's own get_day for Feb 3 (not yet re-checked with that specific tool this pass) or OCA/Pravoslavie directly before being marked fully CONFIRMED.

entries.name: Prophet Zechariah
entries.description: Old Testament prophet, one of the Twelve Minor Prophets (520 BC) -- distinct from Zechariah, father of John the Baptist.
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Feb 8, citing Pravoslavie.ru and Ecclesia.gr. Not previously in this corpus at all under this identity -- the existing 'elizabeth-and-zechariah' row (ANG, Nov 5) is a different Zechariah (father of the Forerunner). Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info or OCA before being marked fully CONFIRMED.

entries.name: Saint Photine, the Samaritan Woman
entries.description: The Samaritan Woman who met Christ at Jacob's Well (John 4), venerated in Orthodox tradition as an Equal-to-the-Apostles martyr.
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Feb 26. A major, universally-known Gospel figure (the Samaritan Woman at the Well, John 4) with no entry at all in this corpus previously -- a genuine gap, not a minor local figure. Date corrected to Mar 20 per OCA (oca.org/saints/lives) -- Feb 26 is specifically the Greek-tradition date; this project's governing EOR source is the Slavic/OCA reckoning (established 2026-09-05). She is also kept on the moveable 'Sunday of the Samaritan Woman' (5th Sunday of Pascha) in all traditions -- a separate, not-yet-built moveable observance this row does not attempt to represent.

entries.name: Righteous Aaron the High Priest
entries.description: Brother of the Prophet Moses and first High Priest of Israel (Exodus/Numbers).
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Mar 12. A major Old Testament figure (brother of Moses, first High Priest) with no entry at all in this corpus previously. Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info or OCA before being marked fully CONFIRMED.

entries.name: Venerable Martyr Eudokia of Heliopolis
entries.description: Reformed courtesan and martyr of Heliopolis in Phoenicia (2nd century).
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Mar 1, citing Pravoslavie.ru. A well-attested and reasonably well-known Byzantine venerable-martyr with no entry at all in this corpus previously. Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info or OCA before being marked fully CONFIRMED.

entries.name: Venerable Paul the Simple
entries.description: Disciple of St. Anthony the Great in Egypt (4th century), known from the Sayings of the Desert Fathers.
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Mar 7, citing Pravoslavie.ru. A well-known figure from the desert-fathers tradition (Sayings of the Desert Fathers) with no entry at all in this corpus previously. Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info or OCA before being marked fully CONFIRMED.

entries.name: Righteous Joseph the Fair
entries.description: Joseph the Patriarch, son of Jacob, sold into slavery in Egypt by his brothers (Genesis 37-50) -- distinct from Joseph the Betrothed, spouse of the Virgin Mary.
entries.ruleSource: ADDED 2026-09-07: found via Wikipedia's compiled Eastern Orthodox liturgics page for Mar 31, which lists him under this fixed civil date (distinct from his separate liturgical prominence in the moveable Holy Monday Gospel readings, which this row does not attempt to represent). A major Old Testament figure with no entry at all in this corpus previously. Needs direct confirmation against orthocal.info or OCA before being marked fully CONFIRMED.
